meaning_simple_english: You say this when you see a person.
You say this when a person goes away.
A short friendly hello.
common_mistakes: Very informal for first meetings with older people.

meaning_simple_english: A short friendly goodbye.
You say this when the answer is true.
example_1: Are you Anna? Yes, I am.
example_2: Do you like tea? Yes, I do.
common_mistakes: Use the full short answer, not only yes.

meaning_simple_english: You say this when the answer is not true.
example_1: Are you Sam? No, I am not.
example_2: Do you like coffee? No, I do not.
collocations: no thank you; no, I am not
common_mistakes: No, I am no (wrong word order).

meaning_simple_english: The person who speaks: me.
common_mistakes: Always a big letter: I, not i.

meaning_simple_english: The person who listens: not me.
common_mistakes: One word for one person or many people.

meaning_simple_english: Be with I. It joins I and a name or word.
collocations: I am + name; I am + adjective

meaning_simple_english: Be with you. It joins you and a name or word.
collocations: you are + name; you are + adjective

meaning_simple_english: Of me. It comes before a thing.
common_mistakes: My name is (not My name Anna).

meaning_simple_english: Of you. It comes before a thing.
The word for a person. Anna is a name.
collocations: my name; first name; your name
common_mistakes: Name needs a or my before it.

meaning_simple_english: You ask this to learn a thing or name.
common_mistakes: Word order: What is your name?

meaning_simple_english: Be with he/she/it and one thing.
One thing; you say it before a word.
collocations: a book; a pen; a name

meaning_simple_english: One thing; you say it before a vowel sound.
Many pages. You read it.
You write with it.
You put things in it. You carry it.
You open it and go in or out.
collocations: open the door; close the door

meaning_simple_english: A kind word. You say it when you ask.
Kind words. You say them when a person helps you.
common_mistakes: Thanks is informal; thank you is safe.

meaning_simple_english: You say this when a bad thing is your fault.
collocations: I am sorry; sorry about that

meaning_simple_english: The near thing. Here, not there.
A person you like. You see them many times.
collocations: my friend; good friend; best friend

meaning_simple_english: The first part of the day. Good morning = hello in the morning.
example_2: I drink tea in the morning.

meaning_simple_english: Nice; not bad.
collocations: good morning; good evening; very good

meaning_simple_english: The last part of the day, before night.
The dark time. You sleep. Good night = goodbye at night.
common_mistakes: Good night is goodbye, never hello.
